refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: The flatpak config command shows or modifies the configuration of a flatpak installation. The following keys are supported:

listitem.para: The languages that are included when installing Locale extensions. The value is a semicolon-separated list of two-letter language codes, or one of the special values * or *all*. If this key is unset, flatpak defaults to including the extra-languages key and the current locale.

This key is used when languages is not set, and it defines extra locale extensions on top of the system configured languages. The value is a semicolon-separated list of locale identifiers (language, optional locale, optional codeset, optional modifier) as documented by setlocale3 (for example, en;en_DK;zh_HK.big5hkscs;uz_UZ.utf8@cyrillic).

If this key is set to false or the no-report-os-info file exists at FLATPAK_CONFIG_DIR Flatpak will not report the OS name, version, and architecture from /etc/os-release to the Flatpak remote via the Flatpak-Os-Info HTTP header when pulling objects. The default value of the key if unset is true.

refsect1.para: Flatpak also supports central, system-managed configuration in /etc/flatpak/config and /etc/flatpak/config.d/*.conf. These files use an ini-style format with a [core] group. The following central keys are supported:

listitem.para: If set to true, central repository policy is enforced, and user-controlled directory overrides via FLATPAK_*_DIR environment variables are ignored with a warning.
If set to false while config-lockdown is enabled, users cannot add or modify user-defined remotes. Centrally configured remotes remain available.

refsect1.para: When central lockdown is enabled, remote definitions from /etc/flatpak/user.remotes.d/*.flatpakrepo are applied to user installations as centrally managed remotes.

To add a centrally managed remote, create a .flatpakrepo file in /etc/flatpak/user.remotes.d/. Each file must contain an exact [Flatpak Repo] group header. The group name is fixed and must not be replaced with a per-remote name. The file should contain the remote URL and, when GPG verification is enabled, either the public key material for the remote using the GPGKey field, or a path to a key file using the GPGKeyFile field. Flatpak imports that key into each installation when the remote is first applied, so clients pick up both the remote definition and its trust root automatically.

listitem.para: Export the remote's ASCII-armored public key.

Either base64-encode the exported key and place the result in the GPGKey field of a /etc/flatpak/user.remotes.d/NAME.flatpakrepo file, or store the key on disk and reference it with GPGKeyFile, together with the Url and any desired metadata.
Ensure /etc/flatpak/config or a file in /etc/flatpak/config.d/ enables [core] config-lockdown=true and configures allow-user-remotes=false if users must not add their own remotes.

Ask users to run any Flatpak command that opens their installation, such as flatpak remotes. On first access, Flatpak loads the central remote into the local repository configuration and imports the bundled GPG key.

refsect1.para: When central lockdown is enabled, Flatpak re-checks centrally managed remotes whenever the user installation is opened. If a user has manually changed the local remote URL, GPG verification settings, or similar repository configuration in their home directory, Flatpak overwrites those local changes from the corresponding /etc/flatpak/user.remotes.d/*.flatpakrepo file. If allow-user-remotes is false, user-defined remotes that are not present in /etc/flatpak/user.remotes.d/ are removed at the same time.

To update a centrally managed remote, edit the corresponding /etc/flatpak/user.remotes.d/NAME.flatpakrepo file and update its GPGKey or GPGKeyFile if the trust root changes. Existing users pick up the new values the next time a Flatpak command opens their installation.
refsect1.programlisting: [Flatpak Repo] Title=Example Central Remote Url=https://example.invalid/repo/ GPGKey=mQINBGexample...
